title: No space left on device - find which disk or tmpfs is full
summary: The message 'No space left on device' means a disk, partition or RAM-based temporary folder has no free room left. These commands show which disk is full and which folders take the most space.

aliases.text: why is my disk full linux
cannot write file no space left
check C drive space like windows
нет свободного места на диске linux
no space left on device ошибка

prerequisites: The copy, download or build that failed had a folder it was writing to

steps.explain: Show every mounted disk with its size, used space, free space and Use%. Find the row with Use% 100% and Avail 0: that disk is full. Rows for /tmp or /dev/shm are RAM disks and can fill up quickly.
steps.expect: A table with Filesystem, Size, Used, Avail, Use%, Mounted on. The full disk shows Use% 100% and Avail 0.

alternatives.explain: Show only the disk that holds one folder, such as the folder where the copy, download or build failed.

placeholders.name: FOLDER
placeholders.description: Folder where the failed copy, download or build was writing

alternatives.expect: One row for the disk that holds that folder.

alternatives.explain: Check /tmp directly. On many systems /tmp is a small RAM disk (tmpfs) that fills up during builds and large downloads.
alternatives.expect: If /tmp is its own RAM disk, a tmpfs row with Mounted on /tmp appears; Use% 100% and Avail 0 means /tmp is full. Otherwise /tmp shares the root disk row.

steps.explain: Check inode usage. A disk can also report 'No space left on device' when it has too many small files, even if df -h shows free bytes. Look at IUse%.
steps.expect: A table with Inodes, IUsed, IFree, IUse%, Mounted on. IUse% 100% on the full disk means too many files, not too many bytes.

steps.explain: List the folders inside the full disk that use the most space, largest first. -x keeps du on one disk so it does not walk into other disks.

placeholders.name: FOLDER
placeholders.description: A folder on the full disk, usually its mount point from df -h

steps.expect: Up to 10 lines: a size and a folder path, largest first. Permission denied messages for system folders can be ignored.

verify.expect: After you free space, the full disk shows Avail above 0 and Use% below 100%.

source.title: df manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
